summary: Home Affairs says European passport holders may be eligible for an eVisitor (subclass 651) visa, which is free. Holders of an ETA-eligible passport must use the Australian ETA App to apply for an Electronic Travel Authority (subclass 601); there is a service charge of AUD 20 to use the app. Home Affairs lists the Visitor visa (subclass 600) for tourists, business visitors or to visit family for 3, 6 or 12 months. For New Zealand citizens, the Special Category visa (subclass 444) is free and is usually applied for each time they enter Australia; an application made on arrival is processed at the airport or seaport.

validityDays.text: The eVisitor visa is valid for travel to Australia for 12 months, starting from the date it is granted.

stayDays.text: You can stay in Australia for 3 months after each entry.

entries.text: The visa has multiple entry. You can leave and re-enter Australia as many times as you want while it is valid.

extendable.text: You can't stay in Australia longer by extending this visa.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Australia?
faq.answer: Yes — an electronic one. United States of America is on Home Affairs' list of ETA-eligible passports, and you must use the Australian ETA App to apply for an ETA if you hold an ETA-eligible passport. There is a service charge of AUD 20 to use the app; Home Affairs says that in most cases it will tell you the result immediately. You can visit as often as you wish in a 12-month period and stay up to 3 months each time you enter.

faq.question: What is the difference between the eVisitor and the Australian ETA?
faq.answer: Home Affairs says both let you visit Australia as often as you wish in a 12-month period and stay up to 3 months each time you enter, to visit family or friends, have a holiday or undertake business visitor activities ("some" business visitor activities on the ETA). The eVisitor (subclass 651) is free, and European passport holders may be eligible for it. The ETA (subclass 601) is for holders of an ETA-eligible passport, who must apply through the Australian ETA App; there is a service charge of AUD 20 to use the app.

faq.question: Do New Zealanders need a visa for Australia?
faq.answer: Home Affairs says the Special Category visa (subclass 444) allows New Zealand citizens who meet the eligibility criteria to visit, study, stay and work in Australia, and is usually applied for each time they enter Australia. It is free, and an application made on arrival is processed at the airport or seaport. It lets them enter and stay in Australia for as long as they are a New Zealand citizen; when they leave Australia the visa ceases.

faq.question: Can I bring food into Australia?
faq.answer: Yes, if it is a risk good. Australia's Department of Agriculture says you must complete a declaration and either declare any risk goods, including food, animal products and plant material, or dispose of them in the bins at the airport or cruise terminal. Declared risk goods are inspected by a biosecurity officer, who may direct them for treatment, export or destruction; goods that do not pose a biosecurity risk are returned. False or misleading information can bring an infringement notice of up to $7,280, civil penalty proceedings or prosecution, and your visa may be cancelled.

faq.question: Can I stay in Australia longer than 3 months as a tourist?
faq.answer: Not on an eVisitor or ETA: Home Affairs says you can stay in Australia for 3 months after each entry, you can't stay longer by extending either visa, and if you want to stay longer than 3 months at a time you must apply for a different visa. For the Visitor visa (subclass 600) Tourist stream, Home Affairs says it generally grants a stay period of 3 months and might grant a stay of up to 12 months in certain circumstances.
